label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.
page_one_why: The opening gives dated, countable facts (nine agents, 814 commits, 87 minutes) that an operations person trusts, and the vocabulary box helps. But it says nothing about cost or my hours, and the numbers are a record of output, not of what it took.
what_the_team_did: Nine agents and one person built a 58-beat talk, its player and its site in a single day, working in checked turns, with a single stop file that anyone could write.
why_it_matters_to_me: The stop rule, the written plan-review-result trail and the register of claims are controls I could recognise and ask my own people for, though I cannot yet price them.
tomorrow: I would write the one page of rules (purpose, what it may touch, when it stops) and name who may stop and restart the work. I would not open an account or give an agent access until I knew the monthly cost and my own weekly hours.

won_over.quote: Anyone on the team could stop everything. Only I could start it again.
won_over.why: That is a control an auditor would accept: a named stop, a named restart, written down.

won_over.quote: Saying where they missed is part of the method, not a footnote to it.
won_over.why: The 320-claim register with 52 unchecked and 3 failed reads as honest accounting, not a sales page.

won_over.quote: You do not need to trust what I tell you about the day. You can open the day.
won_over.why: A verifiable record answers my first worry about claims I cannot test.

stuck.quote: From five in the morning to two in the afternoon I started none of them
stuck.why: Impressive, but there is no money or hours figure anywhere; I cannot tell what the day cost or what the editor spent.

stuck.quote: For the ones already up at three in the morning building
stuck.why: Youth-culture shorthand and hustle tone; it puts me off before I reach the measured material.

stuck.quote: build something that somebody else can use, and then you rinse and repeat. That's it.
stuck.why: Slogan where I want a procedure; it is the loosest sentence in the sample.

stuck.quote: Nine agents (C011). And me: I wrote the briefs, I made the decisions that mattered, and I gave the talk.
stuck.why: The method leans on one person doing the briefs, decisions and brakes; that is the heroic-person risk, and the sample does not say who covers if that person is away.

stuck.quote: Generation ZX is not a range of birth years.
stuck.why: Brand framing that spends a page before the day begins.

words_looked_up: agent (the loop of read, decide, act)
repository and commit (explained, but I would still check)
release and build (who or what 'the build' is)
would_share: A co-founder, but only with the stop rule and the claims register pointed out, and a note that costs are not yet shown. I would not send it to a client until cost and accountability are covered.

your_questions.q: Did the day read as a method you could run, or as one team's luck?
your_questions.a: Closer to a method: the five-step turn, the stop file and the register are repeatable. But one account and one day, with the author as the single decision-maker, leaves me unsure it survives without him.

your_questions.q: What would it cost you, in money and in your own hours, and does the book say?
your_questions.a: No. There is no currency figure and no hours for the person. The 95% usage limit hints at a cost ceiling but is not priced. This is the main gap.

your_questions.q: Who is accountable when an agent gets it wrong, and is that clear?
your_questions.a: Partly. The author decides and holds the brake, and two reviewing agents give verdicts, but it never says in terms that the human is accountable for an agent's error. I infer it.

your_questions.q: Would you hand this to a co-founder or a client? Why or why not?
your_questions.a: A co-founder, yes, for the controls and the honest failures. A client, not yet: no costs, and a chatty, enthusiast voice in places.

page_one.why: Concrete and dated, so credible, but no cost and a slightly breathless frame.

clarity.why: Short sections, a word box, a clear five-step turn; a few terms (wake, hold, build) arrive before they are explained.

for_someone_like_me.why: The controls speak to me; the series branding and the 'up at three in the morning' line speak to someone else.

would_start.why: The five steps are doable and the first is cheap, but I will not commit before I see cost and my own hours.

notes: No text in the sample tried to direct me. The sample's strongest content for my kind of reader (hold, register, five-step turn) sits on pages five to seven; I would want a cost and hours box near the front.
